notes: Two related-but-independent visual features, wired up from a design-tool handoff (dice3d.js + cockpit-surround.css) rather than built from scratch here. 1) 3D dice pop-up: rolling any dice mode (D&D, Alien RPG including stress dice, Blade Runner) can briefly play a real WebGL 3D dice-tumble animation over the map, visible to EVERYONE in the room regardless of which sidebar tab they're on (Board stays mounted always, so it's not gated to the Dice tab) - it always lands on the same result the existing 2D tray/log already show, since the server still decides the roll and the 3D layer is purely presentational. A 'Off / Potato / High' quality setting sits next to the existing dice-skin picker; Off renders nothing (falls back to the 2D tray exactly as before), and it also silently no-ops if WebGL init fails for any reason (no crash). 2) Sci-fi cockpit surround: the sci-fi theme's board+sidebar now sit inside an armoured console housing (rivets, rounded CRT bezel with a slow refresh sweep, grime overlay) layered ON TOP of the existing terminal-green styling, not replacing it - the Classic theme has zero new classes/effects, completely untouched. To test: on any room, go to the Dice tab, confirm the '3D dice pop-up' setting defaults to High, roll a d20 and confirm a 3D die pops up over the map showing the same number as the 2D tray, then confirm a second player who is NOT on the Dice tab (e.g. sitting on Chat) also sees it pop up without switching tabs. Set the setting to Off and confirm rolling shows no 3D overlay at all, just the 2D tray as before. Try Alien RPG (with at least one stress die) and Blade Runner rolls too. Separately, create a sci-fi-themed room and confirm the board/sidebar now have the console housing look (rivets down the sidebar's left edge, rounded glowing bezel around the map, a faint moving scanline sweep) while a Classic-themed room looks exactly as it always has.
